title: Kemer, Phaselis & Tahtalı Mountain: Pine-Fringed Mediterranean

quickAnswer: South of Antalya, the Kemer coastline pairs pine-covered Beydağları peaks with ancient Phaselis's three swimmable harbours and the Olympos Teleferik cable car up 2,365-metre Mount Tahtalı. Situated roughly 58 km from Antalya Airport, the area rewards travellers who trade central resort strips for quieter southern coves like Çıralı and Maden Koyu.

body.text: Why are the coastal ruins of Phaselis unique for swimming?

Phaselis stands on a narrow pine-shaded peninsula flanked by three ancient harbours—North, Central (Military), and South—allowing visitors to walk a Roman colonnaded avenue and step straight into calm, clear water beside ruined quays and aqueducts. Unlike fenced inland excavations, archaeology and swimming share the exact same shoreline.

Founded around 690 BC by Rhodian colonists and visited by Roman Emperor Hadrian in AD 129, [Phaselis Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/Language/Index/EN?url=%2Fmuze-detay%3FsectionId%3DPHS01%26distId%3DPHS) preserves a 25-metre-wide paved main street, two Roman baths, a compact theatre, and towering aqueduct arches that carried spring water down from Mount Tahtalı. The Central Harbour forms a sheltered, shallow lagoon ideal for morning swims, while the wider South Harbour faces the Taurus massif directly behind the pine canopy. Arrive shortly after the 08:00 gate opening to walk the stone street in cool shade before excursion boats anchor offshore around midday.
How does the Olympos Teleferik cable car up Mount Tahtalı work?

The [Olympos Teleferik](https://www.olymposteleferik.com/en/index.html) lifts passengers from its lower station at 726 metres to the 2,365-metre summit of Mount Tahtalı (ancient Mount Olympos) in roughly 10 minutes each way. Cabins glide above cedar forests and bare limestone scree, delivering 360-degree views stretching from Finike to Antalya Bay on clear mornings.

The access road branches inland off the D400 highway between Tekirova and Çamyuva, climbing through Beydağları Coastal National Park to the lower terminal. Per the [Olympos Teleferik timetable notice](https://www.olymposteleferik.com/en/departuretimes.html), the last vehicle entry to the private approach road closes 15 minutes before the final cabin departs, so check seasonal hours before setting out. Summit temperatures routinely sit 10–15°C cooler than the beach; even in August, a light windproof layer makes lingering on the terrace far more comfortable.

items: Visit Phaselis at 08:00–10:30 AM for quiet ruins and calm morning water before tour boats arrive.
Check cloud cover on Mount Tahtalı's peak before driving up to the lower cable-car station.
Pack sturdy sandals for Phaselis's smooth ancient flagstones and a light jacket for the 2,365-metre summit.
Carry water and simple snacks, as food choices inside the Phaselis archaeological park are limited.

body.text: Which Kemer bays are quieter than big resort zones?

To avoid the all-inclusive strips of Beldibi, Göynük, and central Kemer, head south past Tekirova toward Çıralı, Adrasan, and roadless Lycian Way coves such as Maden Koyu (Atbükü). Strict environmental zoning and sea-turtle nesting protections keep buildings low-rise and beach music absent across this southern stretch.

Çıralı offers a 3.2-kilometre pebble-and-sand bay backed by orange groves, family-run bungalows, the ancient ruins of Olympos, and the eternal natural gas flames of Yanartaş (Chimaera). Hikers following the [Tekirova–Maden Koyu–Çıralı coastal stage](https://www.ultratdk.com/rota/123) of the Lycian Way reach Maden Koyu—a pine-rimmed bay beside an abandoned chrome mine—accessible only on foot, by boat, or via rough forest track. Further south, Adrasan Bay curves into a wide, calm horseshoe suited to unhurried mornings and day boats heading out to Suluada.

body.text: How far is Kemer from Antalya Airport?

Kemer town centre lies roughly 55–60 km southwest of Antalya Airport (AYT), a straightforward 1-hour drive along the Antalya ring road and the scenic coastal D400 tunnels. Sub-districts sit closer or farther along the same corridor: Beldibi is about 45 km (40–55 minutes), while Phaselis and Tekirova take 70–80 minutes.

As outlined in [Antalya Airport transfer guides](https://antalyaexperiences.com/antalya-airport-to-kemer-transfer/), private transfers and rental cars are far simpler than public transit because direct municipal buses do not run from the airport terminal to Kemer. Budget travellers take the AntRay tram or Havaş shuttle to Antalya Otogar, then board a frequent Kemer–Kumluca minibus. Anyone using a kemer phaselis guide to stay in Çıralı or Adrasan should budget 90 minutes from AYT and consider renting a car for full independence.

faq.q: Is Phaselis covered by the MuseumPass Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes. Phaselis is operated by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, so both MuseumPass Türkiye and MuseumPass The Mediterranean are accepted alongside individual tickets.

faq.q: Can you visit Phaselis and Mount Tahtalı on the same day?
faq.a: Yes. Swim and walk Phaselis in the early morning, break for lunch near Ulupınar's shaded trout streams, and ride Olympos Teleferik in the afternoon if the summit stays clear.

faq.q: Are Kemer beaches sandy or pebbled?
faq.a: Most Kemer beaches, including Phaselis, Tekirova, and Çıralı, consist of smooth pebbles or coarse shingle, which keeps the water unusually clear; water shoes are helpful.

faq.q: Is the Olympos Teleferik open in winter?
faq.a: Yes, it operates year-round weather permitting, and winter or spring visitors often find snow on the 2,365-metre summit just minutes above coastal sunshine.

faq.q: Which base is better for independent travellers: Kemer town or Çıralı?
faq.a: Çıralı suits independent travellers seeking quiet guesthouses and nature, while central Kemer is convenient mainly for marina boat departures and supermarket access.

faq.q: How does Kemer pair with nearby Mediterranean stops?
faq.a: Kemer links easily east toward [Alanya's Seljuk fortress](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/alanya-travel-guide) or north into the highland lakes of [Eğirdir and Isparta](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/isparta-rose-harvest-egirdir).
